MWCC GC 1.2.5. A bare `#pragma reset` DOES NOT close a `#pragma opt_propagation off` region: the option stays off for the remainder of the translation unit, so every function DEFINED AFTER that line is compiled with propagation off whether or not anyone intended it. Measured in src/game/enemy/enemy.c, where do_enemies' body opens `#pragma opt_propagation off` around one `if (gBoss398 >= 0)` block and closes it with `#pragma reset` (pre-reorder lines 6796/6800).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TYPO, and why it is filed as a law rather than a bug: the region a leaked pragma covers is DEFINITION ORDER, so a .text source-definition reorder (tools/gdl/textorder.py's cure) SILENTLY RELOCATES IT. Before run 52's reorder do_enemies sat at source line 6786 of 7521 and the leak covered four functions (fn_8004D958, fn_8004646C, fn_80046680, init_enemy), all of them tuned to byte-exactness UNDER propagation-off without anyone recording that they depended on it. After the reorder do_enemies is at target-order position 42 of 62 and the same leak covers NINETEEN functions. Two of the newly covered ones regressed and nothing else in the TU moved: damage_enemy real 66 -> 282 (frame 176 -> 160; MWCC CSE'd two int-to-double conversions the target performs separately, deleting `stw`/`stw`/`lfd`/`fsubs`/`fcmpo` and one `fmr`), and fn_8004DF58 EXACT -> STRUCTURAL at 315 against the target's 316 (it lost the target's `addi r29,r3,0` ADDR16_LO home copy at +0x14c). Both returned to their pre-reorder scores under ONE edit -- `#pragma opt_propagation reset` immediately after do_enemies' closing brace -- with no source change to either function. init_enemy then regressed (frame 80 -> 88, 10 aligned IMMEDIATE frame rows, opcode multiset IDENTICAL 136/136) because it had been living inside the leak, and was closed by bracketing it explicitly. `defake_gate.py check game/enemy/enemy.c` printed ZERO rows afterwards.

THE SCREEN, before any text reorder: grep the TU for `#pragma` and pair every `off`/`on` with a matching `<name> reset`. A bare `#pragma reset`, or an opener with no closer at all, means some suffix of the TU is compiled under a non-default option set, and the reorder will move which functions that suffix contains. Bracket each function that depended on the leaked option EXPLICITLY (opener before the definition, `reset` after the closing brace) rather than trying to preserve the accident's extent.

ADDR16_LO COROLLARY, one function, offered to the AL research lane as a zero-build screen rather than as a discriminant: fn_8004DF58 emits the target's ADDR16_LO home copy under DEFAULT propagation and LOSES it under `opt_propagation off`, which is the same direction the class is named for (claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1 -- the copy is what keeps a general temp alive). Any roster member where OURS lacks a home copy the target has is worth checking for a covering `opt_propagation off` region first; that costs one grep. This is ONE observation on ONE function and is NOT offered as the class discriminant.
